t:
Section 5 of the Arts and Artifacts Indemnity Act (20 U.S.C. 974) is amended—
    (1) in subsection (b), by striking “$8,000,000,000” and inserting “$10,000,000,000”; and 
    (2) in subsection (c), by striking “$600,000,000” and inserting “$1,200,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only raises dollar ceilings in the Arts and Artifacts Indemnity Act by striking and inserting figures. The one tempting reading is that indemnity agreements involve outside parties such as museums, but applying for indemnity is not participation, and nothing here creates consultation, a hearing, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: Section 5 of the Arts and Artifacts Indemnity Act (20 U.S.C. 974) is amended

qwen_block.w: This section merely amends statutory dollar limits for indemnity. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely administrative and financial, containing no mechanism for outside participation in decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Section 5 of the Arts and Artifacts Indemnity Act (20 U.S.C. 974) is amended— (1) in subsection (b), by striking “$8,000,000,000” and inserting “$10,000,000,000”; and (2) in subsection (c), by striking “$600,000,000” and inserting “$1,200,000,000”.

opus.w: This section only raises two dollar limits in the Arts and Artifacts Indemnity Act. It does not require consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or any right to sue. Museums and other outside parties do take part in the underlying indemnity program, but only as applicants for a benefit, which does not count as participation. In any case, this amendment does not address that process at all.
opus.s: in subsection (b), by striking “$8,000,000,000” and inserting “$10,000,000,000”

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends statutory dollar limits for indemnity. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as museums, states, or the public) in making the decision to change these limits. The action is a direct legislative amendment without procedural requirements for external input.
qwen_chat.s: Section 5 of the Arts and Artifacts Indemnity Act (20 U.S.C. 974) is amended— (1) in subsection (b), by striking “$8,000,000,000” and inserting “$10,000,000,000”; and (2) in subsection (c), by striking “$600,000,000” and inserting “$1,200,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing indemnity limits affects museums or private entities, thus involving them. However, the text itself only describes a legislative amendment to dollar figures. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. The change is unilateral by Congress.
